thread:
sanjay: Quick sync — I sketched a proto for supporting MIG/fractional-GPU scheduling in Dedicated pools. Want feedback on admission + billing implications.
maria: Nice. Are we talking strict MIG profiles (1g/2g/7g) or more flexible fractional slices?
kevin: Practically we only control MIG profiles exposed by drivers. Flexible slicing would be a software multiplex on top of MIG.
tessa: Product question: customers expect 'dedicated' to mean isolation. Will fractional change our SLAs?
li: It can, but we can offer two modes: Dedicated-FRAC (best-effort isolation, cheaper) and Dedicated-ISOL (full GPU pinned + SLA).
sanjay: Exactly. Proposal: introduce `pool.slice_policy` with values {"none","mig-strict","soft-fraction"}. Admission logic differs per mode.
maria: For `soft-fraction` what's eviction model? If a large job needs entire GPU, do we preempt slices?
kevin: Preemption options: instant force-evict, scheduled drain, or fail-fast admission. I prefer scheduled drain + 30s grace to reduce tail latency.
li: Billing nuance: currently we bill by reserved GPU-hour. For slices we could bill proportional to vGPU time + a fragmentation surcharge.
tessa: Customers will want transparent unit pricing. Can we expose `vGPU-seconds` and an `efficiency` metric per job in console?
sanjay: Yes — add telemetry: `vGPU_seconds`, `physical_gpu_seconds`, `packing_efficiency`. Console can compute effective price.
kevin: Admission pseudocode:
```
if policy == mig-strict: require full-MIG-slot available
elif policy == soft-fraction:
  if packable(slices) -> admit
  elif preemptible_credit > 0 -> attempt preempt
  else -> reject
```
maria: Where does preemptible_credit come from? Tenant-level burst credits or pool-level reclaimable buckets?
li: Mix: tenant gets daily burst credits; operator retains a reclaim pool for emergency preemption. Credits consumed when we preempt other slices.
ops-bot: Reminder: preemption must flip an audit-log event and trigger KMS/ACL refresh for customers — security team flagged this earlier.
tessa: UX: default for new tenants should be `mig-strict` to preserve expectations, opt-in for `soft-fraction` with clear cost savings in docs.
sanjay: One tricky part: headroom. With slices packing tightly, predicting needed headroom for a sudden 7g request is hard. Suggest a conservative warmup_budget metric per pool.
kevin: Implementation: allocator maintains free-slice histogram + quick-evict queue. If a wide request arrives, try drain from queue first, then reclaim credits.
maria: Also quantify accuracy: we need `pack_conflict_rate` telemetry to tune warmup_budget. Start with 3x median arrival until we have data.
li: Compliance: ensure logs show which tenant lost slices on preempt. Also add a policy flag `no-preempt` for regulated customers.
sanjay: Good point. I'll update the proto with fields: `slice_policy`, `warmup_budget_seconds`, `burst_credit_account`, `no_preempt`.
kevin: Let's add a developer hook for a simulated admission run so customers can see success/failure probabilities in console during changes.
tessa: Agree. Next steps: sanjay, can you paste the proto and a short rollout plan? We'll prioritize docs and console visuals.
sanjay: Will do — I'll push a draft RFC to the repo today and attach a simulation script. Thanks for the quick reactions :thumbsup:
